title: Cascade and source order
learningObjectives: Explain how the CSS cascade resolves competing declarations and when source order matters.

understand.concept: The cascade is the browser's decision process for choosing a value when more than one CSS declaration could apply to the same element and property. Source order is one part of that process, not the whole rule.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding the cascade helps you predict styles instead of adding random overrides.
understand.analogy: Imagine several instructions about the same item. The browser follows a defined priority process to decide which instruction wins.
understand.analogyLimit: Unlike a simple queue, CSS also considers origin, importance, cascade layers, specificity and scoping proximity before source order.

explain.narrative: Two matching rules can set the same property. If their cascade priority and specificity are otherwise equal, the declaration that comes later in the relevant order wins. A later low-specificity rule does not automatically beat an earlier high-specificity rule. The browser first sorts declarations by cascade origin and importance, then layers, specificity and (where applicable) scoping proximity; source order breaks a remaining tie.

examples.code: Inspect this paragraph colour.
examples.explanation: The two paragraph rules have equal specificity. The later rule changes the text to dark green. Move the second rule above the first and observe the result.
examples.expectedOutput: The element appears according to the winning CSS rule described in the explanation.

practise.guidedTask: Add a second .notice rule after the first and change only its border colour. Keep the selector unchanged so source order is the deciding factor.
practise.independentTask: Create two equal-specificity rules for a card background. Swap their order and explain why the final colour changes.
hints: Compare declarations for the same element and property.
Check whether the selectors have equal specificity before blaming source order.

questions.prompt: What happens when two declarations have equal cascade priority and specificity?
questions.explanation: Source order resolves the remaining tie.

questions.prompt: Does a later element selector always beat an earlier class selector?
questions.explanation: A class selector has greater specificity than an element selector.
